newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks close just firm after late drift.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks close just firm after late drift.

text.p: Australian shares finished a touch higher as investors mostly ignored the solid performance from the Dow after a benign address to a U.S. senate committee by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index finished 3.2 points up at 2,433.5, 10 points off its intra-day high of 2,443.5.
The market got off to a reasonable start but started to drift after lunch as buying for bellwether issue BHP gradually evaporated.
BHP shares closed 10 cents weaker at A$18.25 (US$14.24) after earlier trading as high as A$18.46.

"Investors are still worried about BHP which has lagged the market since the middle of last year. They are waiting to see more concrete signs of a recovery for the big Australian," a dealer from a Brisbane-based brokerage said.
Another negative factor was the S&P 500 March futures contract which drifted into negative territory late in the Australian session, the dealer said.
He said the market would likely have finished lower on the day except for some late buying interest in major bank issues which had trailed the market for most of the session.

The gold sector saw the most excitement on the day with big turnover and a hefty rise in Mt Edon Gold Mines stock during the day. A joint takeover for the company by Camelot Resources and Canadian group Teck Corp at A$2.15 a share was announced after the close of trade.
Mt Edon shares closed up 64 cents at A$2.08.
However, Papua New Guinean gold miner Goldfields slipped after announcing a further earnings downgrade.
Goldfields shares closed 11 cents weaker at A$2.18.
